name: ULN2803 8-channel Darlington driver
description: TI ULN2803A: eight NPN Darlington low-side switches (open collector, 50 V, 500 mA per channel) with a 2.7 kOhm base resistor per input and common-cathode flyback clamp diodes, so a 3.3 V or 5 V GPIO can switch relays, solenoids, lamps, LED strips or a unipolar stepper. Input nB high = output nC sinks current to GND. No logic supply: COM goes to the load supply for the clamp diodes. Sold as: Texas Instruments ULN2803AN bare chip in a DIP-18 package (pins 1-8 inputs 1B-8B, 9 GND, 10 COM, 11-18 outputs 8C-1C), plugged straight into a breadboard.
eli5: Eight heavy-duty switches in one chip: your board's tiny pin signal turns on a motor, relay or lamp that needs much more current than the pin can give.

buildNotes: Pin 1 (1B) is next to the notch/dot. Inputs 1B-8B are on one side (pins 1-8), outputs 8C-1C on the other (pins 11-18); output nC sits directly opposite input nB.
Wire each load between the load supply (+) and an output nC. The chip only switches the low side; it never sources current.
Connect COM (pin 10) to the load supply (+) whenever the loads are inductive (relays, solenoids, motors): that is how the built-in clamp diodes catch the flyback spike.
Join GND (pin 9) to the microcontroller GND and the load supply (-). All the load current flows out of pin 9, so use a short, thick wire.
3.3 V GPIOs drive it directly: TI specifies VI(on) at most 2.4 V for 200 mA and 2.7 V for 250 mA. Each input draws under about 1 mA.
Expect about 1 V drop across an on output (VCE(sat) 1.0 V typ. at 200 mA, 1.3 V at 350 mA), so a 5 V load sees about 4 V.

500 mA per channel is the absolute maximum for one channel; with all eight on together the package heats up fast - keep the total well under 1 A, or check the datasheet's duty-cycle limits. Two channels can be paralleled for more current.
Unused inputs can be left open (internal resistors hold them off).

example.code:
import time
from uln2803 import ULN2803

# Inputs 1B..8B in order; output nC sinks current while nB is high.
drv = ULN2803([{1B}, {2B}, {3B}, {4B}, {5B}, {6B}, {7B}, {8B}])
drv.write(0b00000101)  # channels 1 and 3 on
print('ON=%s' % '{:08b}'.format(drv.value()))
time.sleep(4)
drv.write(0b10000010)  # channels 2 and 8 on
print('ON=%s' % '{:08b}'.format(drv.value()))
while True:
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Switches channels 1 and 3 on, then channels 2 and 8
